scope: Node VM of actual explorer planning/apply/preview callbacks, using a minimal host facade. No DOM/CSS interaction, OS filesystem or Windows filesystem was executed; case-insensitive expectations model the requested Windows behavior.

tests.name: Windows invalid, reserved, absolute and traversal paths are rejected
Literal bulk rename preserves directory and exact source snapshot
Case-insensitive existing target collision blocks a bulk operation
Multiple moved files cannot collide at one target
Case-only rename is allowed for the same source on Windows
No-op and empty rename plans cannot be applied
A file cannot become an ancestor directory of another file
A target file cannot replace an existing directory hierarchy
Applying a reviewed rename migrates dirty text, saved baseline, tabs, breakpoints and view
Swapping two filenames applies from captured sources, not partially overwritten files
Changed source after preview blocks the entire batch without partial rename
A newly occupied target after preview is detected on apply
Switching project rejects a stale preview callback
Replacing the owner file map rejects a stale preview even with matching strings
Missing source from a folder preview cannot be recreated as undefined
Undo restores paths and metadata once, and cannot silently become redo
Undo cannot overwrite a later edit made to the renamed file
New file rejects both ancestor and descendant file-directory conflicts
Duplicate names are chosen case-insensitively without overwriting existing files
Single-file rename has a direct name field, preview and preserved dirty buffer
Confirmed delete removes only selected files and their editor metadata
Delete confirmation refuses edits made after the confirmation opened
Explorer selection and configuration belong to the selected project
Ctrl selection toggles without navigating or replacing the active editor
Explorer excludes generated directories by default and reveals them explicitly
Every button has one class attribute and escaped filename content
